samples.text: Business continuity plans earn their cost in the hours when a service is degraded but not yet lost. A useful plan tells a manager what can continue, on what basis, and for how long that basis holds. It also names the evidence that would end the interim arrangement. Provisional output deserves a provisional label. Teams that publish interim figures must mark them as interim in the data itself, not only in an email, so a later reader cannot mistake them for final values. A flag on the dataset and a note in the catalogue cost little. Decide in advance who can authorise an interim arrangement, and record each authorisation with its time and scope. Waiting is also a decision, and it deserves the same record as any other. Service owners who choose to wait must note what they expect to change, and by when, so the choice can be reviewed later. Reference data is the quiet dependency in most agency data platforms. Code tables, crosswalks between old and new identifiers, and lookup lists sit under every report and every downstream feed. Yet they rarely receive the engineering discipline that application code gets. A crosswalk edited by hand, with no named owner and no second reviewer, behaves like an unreviewed production change. Anyone with write access can make that change at any hour. Where two identifier schemes remain in use side by side, the crosswalk becomes the single point that translates meaning, and one wrong row Treat each mapping table as code. In practice that means version control for the table and a change request for every edit. It means an automated check that every legacy code resolves to exactly one current code, plus a reviewer who did not make the change. It also means a named owner in the data catalogue, recorded against the table itself and not against whichever team happens to run the pipeline.
